subject: vulture flying
title: In 1876, Chunks of Raw Meat Fell From a Clear Sky Over Kentucky

scenes.text: In 1876, it rained meat in Kentucky.
A farmer's wife was outside making soap when chunks of flesh began falling from a clear, sunny sky.
It went on for several minutes and covered a strip of ground 100 yards long.
Two men tasted it. Mutton, they said, or venison.
Scientists put samples under the microscope and found lung tissue, muscle and cartilage.
The best explanation is still the oldest. Vultures were passing overhead, and vultures throw up in flight. When one starts, the rest join in.

description:
On 3 March 1876, pieces of raw meat fell from a clear sky over a farm in Bath County, Kentucky.
A woman making soap in her yard saw the flesh come down for several minutes, covering an area about 100 yards long and 50 wide. Two men who tasted it judged it to be mutton or venison. Scientists who examined samples identified lung tissue, from either a horse or a human infant, along with muscle fibers and cartilage. The leading explanation, first suggested at the time, is that a flock of vultures disgorged a recent meal while flying over: vultures vomit to lighten their load or deter predators, and when one does, others tend to follow. A preserved piece is still kept at Transylvania University in Lexington.
Would you have tasted it? Comment below.
first_comment: One early theory said it was not meat at all but Nostoc, a jelly-like colony of bacteria. Would you have tasted it?
